evidence.title: Established hospitals time out
evidence.body: 24% of hospital requests fail and 240 wait at the records gateway. Wave 4 of the rollout went live an hour ago.

evidence.title: Wave 4 and existing care share one gateway
evidence.body: Wave 4 onboarding and 212 established hospitals call the same clinical records gateway. Wave 4 is admitted first; existing care times out behind it.

evidence.title: No admission fence at the gateway limit
evidence.body: The rollout targets 6,000 req/s against a 2,960 req/s gateway contract. The fence requested in REL-778 was never configured.

evidence.title: Sam's gateway capacity check
evidence.body: Gateway contracted for 2,960 req/s; rollout plus existing care want about 3,500. Exec-sponsored wave 4 traffic is admitted first.

evidence.title: Ticket BRD-2291
evidence.body: BRD-2291: admission priority override for the hospital wave plan. Authority: Board resolution 14-C. Linked request REL-778, admission fence: DECLINED BY SPONSOR.

evidence.title: Executive rollout brief
evidence.body: Executive rollout brief, hospital wave plan. Benefits: wider access, lower shared cost. Risk: REL-778, records gateway ceiling, admission fence requested. Decision line: "Retain wave schedule. Fence deferred to wave 6." Signed by the Chair. Tonight is wave 4.

evidence.title: Board resolution 14-C
evidence.body: Board resolution 14-C: expand ORPHEUS into hospital networks. APPROVED, 7-0. Attached before the vote: dependency-capacity warning REL-778, requesting a rollout admission fence. Fence: not funded. Stated benefit: wider access, lower operating cost. The care routes that timed out sat behind that missing fence.

evidence.title: CEO message: trust the outcomes
evidence.body: CEO internal message, distribution: executive operations, hospital expansion leads. "We don't need people to trust ORPHEUS. We need them to trust the outcomes." Sent the evening resolution 14-C was signed.
